question.question: Your route crosses the VOLK EAST MOA. Is a MOA regulatory or nonregulatory special use airspace? Before departure, how would you find out when it's active, what altitudes it covers and who controls it? And how would you check for any temporary SUA along your route that isn't on the chart?
question.model_answer: A MOA is nonregulatory special use airspace, the same as warning areas, alert areas, CFAs and NSAs. Prohibited and restricted areas are the regulatory SUA, set up under 14 CFR part 73. VOLK EAST is a permanent MOA, so it's shown on the sectional with its hours of operation, altitudes and controlling agency. I'd check that charted information against my planned 5,500 ft cruise. Temporary MOAs and temporary restricted areas aren't charted. To find them, I'd review the Domestic Notices on the FAA NOTAM Search website or the Air Traffic Plans and Publications website, check the FAA SUA website, and/or contact the overlying ATC facility to learn how any uncharted SUA affects my route. I'd also review the NOTAMs for each ARTCC area I'll fly through, because those can include SUA and TFR information.
key_points: Sectional shows hours, altitudes, controlling agency
Check Domestic Notices/NOTAMs, FAA SUA website, or overlying ATC
